title: Dashboard provenance and metric lineage notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a pragmatic approach for attaching provenance and lineage metadata to key inference observability signals (metrics & traces), plus recommendations for composing dashboards that make provenance visible and actionable to operators. Goal: reduce misattribution, speed root-cause, and make safe metric deprecation/migration easier during rollouts.

Scope:
- Server-side inference metrics (latency, token costs, KV cache stats)
- Trace anchors and minimal-span capture for tenant/session reconstruction
- Dashboard panel metadata, ownership, and query provenance
- Lightweight examples and SQL snippets for lineage queries

Why this matters (examples):
- We get two slightly different p95 implementations (per-request vs per-token) surfaced in different widgets; without provenance people chase the wrong SLI.
- During model rollouts a metric name changes (e.g., inference_latency -> inference_latency_v2) and alerts fire because dashboards still query old field.
- Operators need a quick way from a dashboard panel -> instrumentation PR / data pipeline to see whether metric drift is expected.

Recommended minimal provenance schema (per metric/series):
- metric_id: unique short id (e.g., inf.lat.p95.v1)
- name: human friendly (e.g., p95_inference_latency_ms)
- origin: service name and binary (e.g., runtime-fanout:v1.4.2)
- instrumented_by: GitHub PR / engineer handle (e.g., gh/pr/88, @diego)
- collection_pipeline: exporter -> metrics-proxy -> metrics-db (simple path text)
- schema_version: semantic (v1, v2)
- aggregation_window: how we compute (per-request, per-token, rolling 1m)
- cardinality_hint: low|medium|high (helps dashboard designers)
- last_schema_change: YYYY-MM-DD
Store this metadata in the metric registry (Confluence + a machine-readable index in telemetry repo). Display the most important fields as a compact panel footer on dashboards.

Metric definitions (examples):
1) p95_inference_latency_ms- metric_id: inf.lat.p95.v1- type: latency (histogram-derived)- collection: per-request latency observed in runtime edge before any post-processing or serialization- aggregation: compute 95th percentile over 1m rolling buckets, then report as gauge per 1m- alert suggestion: p95 > 250ms for 5m- instrumentation notes: must include model_id, route, region, tenant_id. Avoid double-counting when fan-out is present: capture root request id as span attribute.- example SQL (PromQL-ish/SQL-ish): SELECT percentile_cont(0.95, latency_ms) FROM inference_request_stats WHERE minute = current_minute GROUP BY model_id, route;

2) token_cost_per_request_usd- metric_id: cost.token.req.v1- type: derived (tokens * cost_per_token)- collection: tokens emitted (from runtime) * cost table (by model+quantization level) applied at aggregation layer- aggregation: sum(cost) / count(requests) by route/tenant over 1h- alert suggestion: per-tenant cost spike > 3x baseline- instrumentation notes: ensure token attribution is bound to request root span to avoid double-charge across retries

3) kv_cache_hit_rate- metric_id: cache.kv.hitrate.v1- type: ratio- collection: instrument KV cache hooks: hits, misses per request; emit per-request hit_count and total_keys_accessed- aggregation: sum(hits) / sum(total) by model_id, shard, and time window (5m)- alert suggestion: sustained drop > 20% vs baseline for 15m- note: report cardinality_hint=high (shard + model + tenant) and provide rollup panels (global & top-ten tenants)

4) session_warmth_index (heuristic)- metric_id: session.warmth.v1- type: derived score (0-100)- definition: 100 * (kv_cache_hits_weighted + prefix_cache_hits_weighted) / expected_keys_accessed- use: quick indicator for whether a session is cold/warm; used to route synthetic probe types or to trigger warming policies- instrumentation: compute at session close or sample periodically; store sample_time and sample_basis (last_n_requests)

5) fallback_rate_to_light_model- metric_id: fallback.lightmodel.rate.v1- type: counter/ratio- collection: increment when runtime routes to fallback_low_cost variant (at routing decision point)- alert suggestion: >1% sustained for high tier customers or sudden delta > 0.5%

Panel metadata practices:
- Every dashboard panel should include (rendered small): metric_id(s), primary_owner (team or individual), last_update (YYYY-MM-DD), query_version (tag or commit hash).
- For derived panels show provenance chain: raw metrics -> transform SQL/Flux/PromQL -> aggregation window. This chain can be shown in a hover tooltip or collapsed metadata footer.
- Add a small ‘investigate’ link on the panel that opens a curated investigation playbook (Confluence) and the exact query used.
- Track and display query cost estimate (approx) for expensive panels; hide by default for non-operator roles.

Tracing guidance (session-friendly, cost-aware):
- Sampling policy: low-severity normal traffic: 1% uniform sampling; high-impact events (fallback routes, model errors, cache-miss spikes): forced sampling (100%) for a short window (30-120s) around anomalies.
- Trace anchors: always collect a compact trace anchor for every request: root_span_id, request_id, model_id, route, tenant_id, tokens_returned (approx). Anchor size should be small (single line log).- Full-span capture: for forced-sampled traces collect full spans and kv access events. Limit full-span TTL in storage (e.g., 72h) and only store references for longer retention.- Trace annotations to prefer: routing_decision, kv_keys_accessed_count, kv_hit_bitmap (compact), cache_shard, model_variant, quantization_profile, fallback_reason, output_size_tokens.

Crosswalk examples (how to jump from metric -> trace):
- Panel shows kv_cache_hit_rate drop for shard s-17 at 2025-02-28 10:11-10:25. Click 'investigate' -> run saved query (see linked_artifacts) that returns top 50 request_ids with low hit counts. Use these request_ids to retrieve trace anchors; request_ids with forced sampling, or present in auxiliary ephemeral trace-store, will have full traces.
- Suggested helper SQL snippet (pseudo):
  SELECT request_id, minute, hit_count, total_keys FROM kv_events WHERE shard = 's-17' AND minute BETWEEN '2025-02-28T10:11' AND '2025-02-28T10:25' ORDER BY hit_count ASC LIMIT 50;

Dashboard design heuristics (to reduce confusion):
- One canonical source per SLI. If multiple teams need the same number, agree on canonical metric_id and publish transforms separately.- Keep raw operational panels (per-shard/per-model) separate from product-facing SLIs (global p95, 99) to avoid accidental alert binding.
- Use color/label conventions to indicate data freshness vs derived: raw = neutral; derived = small label (derived) and tooltip explanation.

Metric lifecycle & deprecation checklist:
- Before change: create a migration plan in Confluence with metric_id mapping table and owners.
- Mark older metric as deprecated in the registry and add deprecation footer on dashboards.
- Provide a bridging transform in metrics-proxy that emits both old_name and new_name for at least one release cycle (2 weeks).- Update alerts and runbooks to reference the new metric_id.
- Remove old metric after deprecation window and confirm via query (no consumers).

Runbook snippet: rollouts and probes
- Pre-rollout:
  - Validate instrumentation PR exists and metadata fields completed (metric_id, instrumented_by, schema_version)
  - Create synthetic probes that cover cold vs warm sessions and peak-length prompts
  - Add short-term increased trace sampling for rollout window (configurable)
- During rollout:
  - Watch p95_inference_latency_ms, fallback_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate in a single monitoring lane
  - Set temporary alert thresholds to be more sensitive (30% of normal) for first 60m
  - Use session_warmth_index panel to observe whether sessions are getting less warm (indicates cache warming problems)
- Post-rollout:
  - Verify metric lineage: ensure dashboards show new metric_id and query_version matches instrumentation PR
  - Run a metric-consumers scan (simple regex against dashboards & alerts) to find remaining references to deprecated metric names

Operational queries & examples (searching lineage):
- Find dashboards that reference a metric id (pseudo):
  SELECT dashboard_id, panel_id FROM dashboard_index WHERE query_text ILIKE '%inf.lat.p95%';
- Find last change for metric by metric_id (pseudo):
  SELECT metric_id, last_schema_change, instrumented_by FROM metric_registry WHERE metric_id = 'cache.kv.hitrate.v1';

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we embed metric provenance as labels on every timeseries (cost vs cardinality tradeoff)?
- How long should we keep full-span traces for forced-sampled events (default 72h OK?)
- Ownership model: metric owner vs panel owner - should we allow separate teams to both be primary owners?

Immediate action items (owners):
- Ava: prototype dashboard footer UI with metric_id + query_version (2wk spike)
- Diego: add metric_registry JSON schema and import script into telemetry repo (PR link above)
- Priya: add synthetic probe templates for cold-session warming scenarios

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the metric_id short and stable; avoid renaming by encoding change via schema_version not renames.
- We want quick jumps from any panel to the code that created the metric (instrumentation PR) — that is the single most time saving improvement for operators.

References/links (saved):
- Metric registry (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/metric-registry
- Telemetry instrumentation repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-instrumentation
- Incident runbook template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/incident-runbook-template

End of draft.
